skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Guides an AI coding assistant through creating isolated Git worktrees, selecting the right directory, checking ignore rules, and verifying a clean baseline.
skill.summary: Create isolated Git worktrees with directory checks, setup steps, and baseline testing.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are markdown shell examples or inline directory names rather than Ruby backtick execution. Two command blocks are confirmed medium risk because setup and test commands can execute project-controlled code. A semantic finding also flags automatic .gitignore changes and commits without a separate approval step.

remediation.issue: Automatic setup and test command execution
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running install, build, or test commands, especially in untrusted repositories.
Ask before editing .gitignore and before creating a commit; show the exact change and proposed commit message.
Document that the global ~/.config location is optional, user selected, and should include cleanup guidance.

remediation.issue: Branch names are used in filesystem paths
remediation.suggestion: Validate branch names before constructing worktree paths to avoid confusing nested or invalid paths.

static_findings.snippet: **If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.

content.value_statement: Feature work can disrupt current branches and make baseline failures hard to trace. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safe Git worktree setup and verification.
actual_capabilities: Selects an existing .worktrees or worktrees directory by documented priority.
Checks CLAUDE.md for a worktree directory preference before asking the user.
Prompts for a directory choice when no project convention exists.
Verifies project-local worktree directories are listed in .gitignore.
Creates a new Git worktree and moves the session into that workspace.
Runs detected setup and baseline test commands for common project ecosystems.
limitations: Requires a Git repository that supports worktrees.
Package install and test commands can execute project-controlled code.
Does not define cleanup steps after work finishes.
Does not fully validate branch names before using them in paths.

use_cases.title: Start Feature Work Safely
use_cases.description: Create an isolated workspace before changing code on a new branch.

use_cases.title: Preserve Review Context
use_cases.description: Keep the current checkout unchanged while an assistant implements a separate task.

use_cases.title: Prepare Baseline Validation
use_cases.description: Run setup and tests before implementation so later failures have a clear comparison point.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Worktree
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one feature branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Git worktrees skill to create an isolated workspace for my next feature. Follow existing project conventions and report the final location.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up and Verify Baseline
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup with dependency and test checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a worktree for this task, run the project setup steps you detect, then run baseline tests and summarize any failures before coding.

prompt_templates.title: Follow Repository Conventions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use in a repository with documented preferences.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the worktree workflow, inspect the repository guidance for directory preferences, and ask before changing ignore files or creating commits.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Parallel Implementation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for multiple isolated branches.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan isolated worktrees for the approved implementation phases, explain the branch names and locations, and wait for confirmation before running setup commands.

output_examples.input: Set up an isolated workspace for an authentication feature.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the selected worktree directory, confirms ignore coverage, creates the feature branch, and summarizes baseline test status.

output_examples.input: Prepare a worktree in a repository with no existing convention.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks where worktrees should be stored before creating anything, then follows the selected location.

output_examples.input: Start work when baseline tests fail.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the failing checks and asks whether to investigate or proceed before implementation begins.

best_practices: Confirm the directory choice when the repository has no clear worktree convention.
Treat setup and test commands as code execution in untrusted repositories.
anti_patterns: Running package installs in untrusted repositories without approval.
Continuing feature work after baseline tests fail without user direction.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps an assistant create an isolated Git worktree before starting feature work.

faq.question: Does it choose the worktree directory automatically?
faq.answer: It first checks existing directories and repository guidance, then asks when no convention exists.

faq.question: Why does it check .gitignore?
faq.answer: The check helps prevent project-local worktree contents from being accidentally tracked.

faq.question: Can setup commands be risky?
faq.answer: Yes. Package installs, builds, and tests can execute code from the repository or dependencies.

faq.question: Does this skill clean up worktrees?
faq.answer: No. It names a related cleanup workflow, but this skill focuses on creation and baseline checks.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
